The visible separation is counted as a gap, not inferred from RAW vertex indices.

Blue slats form the top of a coherent backless bench with substantial end supports. Gray side walls meet the seating level in both oblique views and fixed sections. No obvious detached fragments or redundant upper/lower seat layer.

Blue plate floats high near the top of the gray back while the gray bench seat lies far below. Gray seat has a long triangular opening/tear and uneven strips. Thin legs remain visible and are not called missing solely for being thin; body and C relation are impaired.

Rounded loop-frame bench has blue C at its upper seating region. Curved end supports sweep down to the base; both sections are compatible with this continuous loop form. Open frame voids are intentional rather than scored as missing panels. No clear loose fragments or competing seating surface.

Gray pedestal bench has two substantial supports and an upper tray/plank seating surface. Blue C is embedded below that gray top: side section shows blue near 0.65 crossing the middle of board walls whose top is around 0.8. Thus C is superseded by another seat layer, despite a coherent complete body.

Two oblique views show a regular gray slab-top bench with two substantial end supports. Blue C lies lower and projects in front/side of that gray top; front and side sections separate the blue seating level from the gray seat. The gray body is coherent, but C is not visibly its adopted seating surface. No clear detached gray debris or folded face is resolved.

The gray horizontal top and both end panels form a recognizable supported bench in both oblique views. Blue C protrudes away from and below the gray top. Both fixed sections confirm the offset rather than a continuous C seating surface. No clear separate gray fragment or severe fold is visible.

A largely level gray slab spans two vertical end supports. The blue L-like surface remains at another height and extends away from the slab; the section traces do not put C on the generated seating plane. The visible gray bench remains recognizable without obvious floating debris or a clearly folded panel.

The gray bench has two end supports and a long top, with a narrow longitudinal split/strip visible along the top in the oblique views. That detail does not clearly resolve as detached debris. C remains lower and offset; both sections show its level separated from the gray seat. No unambiguous folded panel is visible.

Both views show an intact-looking gray top with slab-like supports at each end. Blue C extends below and beside this seating surface rather than being continued by it. Front and side traces retain the same clear level/position mismatch. No distinct detached gray piece or pronounced fold is resolved.

The two oblique views show a coherent corner bench: blue C supplies the two meeting seating spans, with gray back panels and visible posts beneath the seat ends/corner. The fixed front and side sections place gray structure around and below the blue seat, rather than another seat replacing it. No clear loose debris or folded seat is visible.

A gray backrest, lower seating span and thick side supports make a recognizable bench. Blue C crosses higher and projects beyond the gray seating span. The front section puts the gray seat below C; the side section places the main gray seating trace away from much of C. No separate debris or definite face fold is resolved.

Both views retain a recognizable backed bench with block-like side support. The blue surface protrudes through the middle/side while the gray seat is visibly lower. Front and side sections preserve this mismatch. The small trace gaps alone do not establish debris or a folded surface.

The gray body consists of a long back, lower seat and substantial side supports. Blue C sits above the gray seating line and its perpendicular portion extends outside the gray seat. Both fixed sections corroborate the separation. No clearly isolated gray fragment or severe folded sheet is visible.

A regular gray backed bench with broad side supports is recognizable in both oblique views. Blue C is displaced above and across the lower gray seat instead of forming its continued surface. Front and side sections show the same offset; no unmistakable loose piece or folded panel is resolved.

The gray back, seat strip and end supports form a plausible bench silhouette. C protrudes at a higher level and to the side, while front/side gray seating traces remain below or away from it. No definite detached gray fragment or self-fold is visible in the four views.

A coherent L-shaped bench is visible from both sides. Blue C forms the meeting seat surfaces, gray back panels rise along them, and posts support the ends and corner. The front and side sections are consistent with gray structure surrounding/supporting the blue level. No obvious loose debris or folded seat is seen.

The blue slatted C remains above a malformed gray assembly. Both oblique views show large slanted/curved sheets, open wedges and a small separated-looking end flap instead of a clear set of legs or sound end supports. The front trace places the main gray span well below C, and the side trace bends/doubles back. Visible tearing/open wedges and folded gray panels undermine the body.

Both oblique views show a regular long bench/table-like body with four slender supports beneath the blue slatted top. The front section places a thin gray support immediately under C, while the side sections follow the individual slat thicknesses. The blue slats remain the exposed usable surface. No clear stray debris or folded layer is visible.

The gray geometry below the blue slats is made of broad warped sheets with a triangular open end and irregular detached-looking flaps. A credible leg/end-support arrangement is not visible. Front and side sections show the principal gray span separated below C and a bent/doubled profile, consistent with the obvious folded and torn-looking body rather than adoption of the slatted top.

Two views reveal a buckled gray lower assembly with large open wedges and end flaps beneath the intact blue slats. The major supports are not legible as functioning legs or continuous end panels. Fixed sections put the gray seating-like span far below C and expose a bent return profile. The visible sheet folding and openings impair the whole body.

The blue slatted plane is elevated above a gray twisted sheet assembly. Both views show an irregular open lower span and a triangular end flap, with no convincing intact support arrangement. The front section separates the gray span from C; the side section shows the gray profile turning down and across underneath. Visible openings/flaps and folded panels remain.

Both oblique views show a usable-looking long bench with blue slats on top, a gray lower seat rim and broad end-panel supports. The front and side sections place most gray structure below the blue slat plane rather than covering it with a substitute top. Some gray outlines are jagged, but no clearly isolated fragment or severe folded sheet is resolved.

The two end-panel supports and long body remain recognizable, but broad gray triangles cover most blue slats and leave an irregular diagonal opening across the top. Both views show the split rather than the intended exposed slatted surface. Front and side sections put a second gray upper layer above C. The jagged top opening and visible superposed layer impair the seat while supports remain present.

A gray slab bench with end supports is visible, but its top contains a long irregular diagonal split and covers the blue slats except through the split and along edges. Front and side section traces show the gray top above the blue C plane. This is a visibly damaged/superposed seating layer rather than clear use of C; the principal end supports survive.

The bench silhouette and two broad end supports are coherent, and the gray top is more nearly filled across its span. That gray top nevertheless blankets nearly all blue slats, leaving mostly blue edges/small gaps visible. Both sections place a gray seating layer just above C, establishing a superposed replacement surface. No separate gray debris or large resolved opening is evident.

The long gray body is supported by end panels, but the top is interrupted by a diagonal torn-looking opening. The blue slats show mainly through this opening and at the margins because broad gray faces cover them. Front and side sections confirm the second gray layer above the C level. Visible top damage and layering impair the body without removing the main supports.

Both oblique views show an orderly bench/table-like form with four thin legs and the blue slats left exposed as the top. The front trace sits just beneath C and the side section follows separate slat thicknesses instead of a new gray cover. No clearly detached fragment, large unintended opening or folded layer is visible.

The gray bench retains both end supports, but broad gray faces create a replacement top with a long diagonal split exposing some blue slats. Both oblique views show the jagged opening; the front and side sections show that gray top above the original blue plane. The visible opening and double surface impair the seat, while the support structure is still present.
